ko.title: [소비자 심리학 #3] 그 광고 음악이 머릿속에서 떠나지 않는 이유: 소비자는 브랜드를 어떻게 배우고 기억하는가

segments.src: > Brands teach us through repeated pairings and rewards, and whether we recall a brand on our own or only recognize it on a shelf changes how we buy.
segments.tr: > 브랜드는 반복된 짝짓기와 보상을 통해 우리를 가르치며, 우리가 브랜드를 스스로 떠올리는지 아니면 진열대에서 알아보기만 하는지에 따라 구매 방식이 달라진다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Nobody is born knowing that a red can means "refreshing" or that a swoosh means "athletic."
segments.tr: 아무도 빨간색이 "상쾌함"을, 나이키 로고(스우시)가 "운동 기능성"을 뜻한다는 것을 태어날 때부터 알고 있지는 않다.

segments.src: We **learn** these links, mostly without trying.
segments.tr: 우리는 대부분 애쓰지 않아도 이런 연결고리를 **학습**한다.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually describe that learning in two ways.
segments.tr: 소비자 심리학자들은 보통 이 학습을 두 가지 방식으로 설명한다.

segments.src: Classical conditioning: learning by association**
segments.tr: 고전적 조건형성: 연상을 통한 학습**

segments.src: In Ivan Pavlov's famous experiments, dogs heard a sound right before getting food.
segments.tr: 이반 파블로프의 유명한 실험에서 개들은 먹이를 받기 직전에 소리를 들었다.

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: 여러 번 짝지어진 뒤에는 소리만 들려도 개들이 침을 흘렸다.

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: 광고도 종종 같은 원리로 작동한다.

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: 중립 자극인 브랜드를 경쾌한 음악, 귀여운 강아지, 웃는 유명인처럼 이미 사람들을 기분 좋게 만드는 것과 함께 보여주면, 그 좋은 기분의 일부가 브랜드에 옮겨갈 수 있다.

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: 반복은 도움이 되지만, 지나치면 사람들이 지루해하거나 짜증을 느끼는 지점인 *마모 효과(wear-out)*를 일으킬 수 있다.

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: 관련된 개념은 **자극 일반화**다. 사람들은 한 대상에 대한 감정을 그것과 비슷해 보이는 것에도 그대로 가져간다.

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: 이것이 바로 PB 상품이 시장 선도 제품과 비슷한 포장을 쓰는 이유이며, 잘 알려진 브랜드가 같은 이름으로 새 제품 라인을 출시할 수 있는 이유이기도 하다.

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: 조작적(도구적) 조건형성: 결과를 통한 학습**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: 여기서는 행동이 그 행동 *이후에* 일어나는 일에 의해 형성된다.

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: 어떤 물건을 사는 것이 훌륭한 제품, 할인, 적립 포인트 같은 보상으로 이어지면, 그 물건을 다시 살 가능성이 높아진다.

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: 멤버십 프로그램, "열 번째 커피는 무료" 스탬프 카드, 깜짝 혜택은 모두 이 원리에 기반한다.

segments.src: **Memory: recall vs.
segments.tr: **기억: 회상 vs.

segments.src: recognition**
segments.tr: 재인**

segments.src: Learning only matters if it sticks.
segments.tr: 학습은 기억에 남아야 의미가 있다.

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:
segments.tr: 마케터들은 브랜드 기억을 두 가지로 구분한다:

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **브랜드 회상**: 아무 힌트 없이 스스로 브랜드 이름을 떠올린다. ("승차 공유 앱을 말해보세요.")

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **브랜드 재인**: 브랜드를 보거나 들었을 때 그것을 알아본다. ("이 로고를 본 적 있나요?")

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: 재인은 회상보다 쉽다.

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: 대부분의 사람은 힌트 없이 이름을 댈 수 있는 것보다 훨씬 많은 브랜드를 알아본다.

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.
segments.tr: 어느 쪽이 더 중요한지는 결정이 내려지는 장소에 따라 달라진다.

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.
segments.tr: 진열대 앞에서 고른다면 재인만으로 충분할 수 있다.

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.
segments.tr: 외출 전에 식당을 고르거나 배관공을 부를 때처럼 미리 결정한다면, 브랜드가 스스로 떠올라야 하므로 회상이 이긴다.

segments.src: The few brands that come to mind for a category are sometimes called the **consideration set**.
segments.tr: 한 카테고리에서 떠오르는 몇 안 되는 브랜드를 **고려 상표 집합(consideration set)**이라고 부르기도 한다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Imagine it's Friday night and a friend texts, "Want to order pizza?"
segments.tr: 금요일 밤, 친구가 "피자 시킬까?"라고 문자를 보냈다고 상상해 보자.

segments.src: Before opening any app, you think of maybe two or three chains.
segments.tr: 어떤 앱을 열기도 전에 머릿속에 두세 개의 체인점이 떠오른다.

segments.src: That is **recall** at work, and the brands that pop up get the first shot at your $25.
segments.tr: 이것이 **회상**이 작동하는 모습이며, 먼저 떠오른 브랜드가 당신의 25달러를 가져갈 첫 기회를 얻는다.

segments.src: Now picture yourself in the cereal aisle at Target.
segments.tr: 이제 타깃(Target) 매장의 시리얼 코너에 서 있다고 상상해 보자.

segments.src: You didn't plan a brand, but a familiar box catches your eye and you think, "Oh, I know that one."
segments.tr: 브랜드를 미리 정하지 않았지만, 익숙한 상자가 눈에 띄고 "아, 이거 알아"라고 생각한다.

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.
segments.tr: 이것이 **재인**이며, 한 시간 전에는 이름조차 말할 수 없었더라도 익숙한 포장이 선택을 얻을 가능성이 높다.

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.
segments.tr: 또 일정 횟수 구매하면 음료 한 잔을 공짜로 주는 커피숍 앱도 있다.

segments.src: Each stamp or point is a small reward that nudges you to come back, which is operant conditioning in your pocket.
segments.tr: 스탬프나 포인트마다 다시 방문하도록 살짝 밀어주는 작은 보상이 쌓이며, 이것이 주머니 속의 조작적 조건형성이다.

segments.src: Add a cheerful seasonal ad with cozy music and fall leaves, and classical conditioning is helping too.
segments.tr: 아늑한 음악과 가을 낙엽이 나오는 밝은 시즌 광고를 더하면, 고전적 조건형성도 함께 작동하고 있는 것이다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Classical conditioning links a brand to feelings by repeatedly pairing it with something people already like.
segments.tr: 1. 고전적 조건형성은 사람들이 이미 좋아하는 것과 브랜드를 반복해서 짝지어 감정을 연결한다.

segments.src: 2. Operant conditioning shapes repeat buying through rewards such as quality, discounts, and loyalty points.
segments.tr: 2. 조작적 조건형성은 품질, 할인, 적립 포인트 같은 보상을 통해 반복 구매를 형성한다.

segments.src: 3. Recall (naming a brand unprompted) is harder than recognition (knowing it when you see it), and which one matters depends on where the decision happens.
segments.tr: 3. 회상(힌트 없이 브랜드 이름 대기)은 재인(보았을 때 알아보기)보다 어렵고, 어느 쪽이 중요한지는 결정이 일어나는 장소에 따라 달라진다.

segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 퀴즈

segments.tr: **Q1.** 탄산음료 광고는 여름 바비큐 파티에서 친구들이 웃는 장면과 함께 브랜드를 항상 보여주며, 시청자가 브랜드에 대해 행복한 감정을 갖기를 기대한다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Classical conditioning**: Learning that happens when a neutral stimulus (like a brand) is repeatedly paired with one that already triggers a response.
segments.tr: - **고전적 조건형성**: 중립 자극(예: 브랜드)이 이미 반응을 일으키는 자극과 반복적으로 짝지어질 때 일어나는 학습.

segments.src: - **Operant conditioning**: Learning in which behavior becomes more or less likely depending on the reward or punishment that follows it.
segments.tr: - **조작적 조건형성**: 뒤따르는 보상이나 처벌에 따라 행동이 더 또는 덜 일어나게 되는 학습.

segments.src: - **Stimulus generalization**: Responding to a similar-looking stimulus the same way as to the original, such as trusting a lookalike package.
segments.tr: - **자극 일반화**: 원래 자극과 비슷해 보이는 자극에 같은 방식으로 반응하는 것. 예를 들어 비슷하게 생긴 포장을 신뢰하는 것.

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: Retrieving a brand name from memory without any cue except the product category.
segments.tr: - **브랜드 회상**: 제품 카테고리 외에는 아무 단서 없이 기억에서 브랜드 이름을 꺼내는 것.

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: Correctly identifying a brand as familiar when it is shown or named.
segments.tr: - **브랜드 재인**: 브랜드가 보이거나 언급되었을 때 그것이 익숙하다고 올바르게 알아보는 것.

zh.title: [消费者心理学 #3] 为什么那段广告旋律总在你脑海里挥之不去：消费者如何学习并记住品牌

segments.src: > Brands teach us through repeated pairings and rewards, and whether we recall a brand on our own or only recognize it on a shelf changes how we buy.
segments.tr: > 品牌通过反复的配对与奖励来教育我们；而我们是自己想起某个品牌，还是只是在货架上认出它，会改变我们的购买方式。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Nobody is born knowing that a red can means "refreshing" or that a swoosh means "athletic."
segments.tr: 没有人天生就知道红色罐子代表“清爽”，或者对勾标志代表“运动”。

segments.src: We **learn** these links, mostly without trying.
segments.tr: 我们几乎是在不经意间**学会**这些联系。

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually describe that learning in two ways.
segments.tr: 消费心理学家通常用两种方式来描述这种学习。

segments.src: Classical conditioning: learning by association**
segments.tr: 经典条件反射：通过联想学习**

segments.src: In Ivan Pavlov's famous experiments, dogs heard a sound right before getting food.
segments.tr: 在伊万·巴甫洛夫著名的实验中，狗在获得食物之前总会先听到一个声音。

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: 经过足够多次的配对后，光是这个声音就会让它们分泌唾液。

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: 广告常常遵循同样的原理。

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: 把品牌（一个中性刺激）与已经能让人感觉良好的事物放在一起，比如欢快的音乐、可爱的小狗或微笑的名人，那么这些好感就有可能转移到品牌身上。

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: 重复有帮助，但重复过度会导致*疲劳*（wear-out），即人们感到厌烦或反感的临界点。

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: 相关的概念是**刺激泛化**：人们会把对某一事物的感受转移到与之相似的事物上。

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么商店自有品牌常使用与市场领导者相似的包装，也是为什么知名品牌可以用同一名称推出新产品线。

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: 操作性（工具性）条件反射：通过结果学习**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: 在这里，行为是由行为*之后*发生的事情塑造的。

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: 如果购买某物会带来奖励，比如优质产品、折扣或积分，你就会更倾向于再次购买。

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: 会员计划、“买满第10杯免费”的集点卡以及惊喜福利，都是建立在这一原理之上的。

segments.src: **Memory: recall vs.
segments.tr: **记忆：回忆 vs.

segments.src: recognition**
segments.tr: 识别**

segments.src: Learning only matters if it sticks.
segments.tr: 学习只有在被记住时才有意义。

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:
segments.tr: 营销人员区分两种品牌记忆：

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **品牌回忆**：你无需任何提示，自己说出品牌名称。（“请说出一个网约车应用。”）

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **品牌识别**：当你看到或听到某个品牌时，能认出它。（“你以前见过这个标志吗？”）

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: 识别比回忆更容易。

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: 大多数人能识别的品牌远多于他们在没有提示的情况下能说出的品牌。

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.
segments.tr: 哪一种更重要，取决于你在哪里做决定。

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.
segments.tr: 如果你是在货架前做选择，识别可能就已足够。

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.
segments.tr: 如果你在出门前就已经决定，比如选餐厅或叫水管工，品牌必须自己浮现在脑海中，因此回忆更占优势。

segments.src: The few brands that come to mind for a category are sometimes called the **consideration set**.
segments.tr: 某个品类中能自然浮现在脑海里的少数品牌，有时被称为**考虑集**。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的例子

segments.src: Imagine it's Friday night and a friend texts, "Want to order pizza?"
segments.tr: 想象一下周五晚上，朋友发来消息：“要不要点披萨？”

segments.src: Before opening any app, you think of maybe two or three chains.
segments.tr: 在打开任何应用之前，你会想到两三家连锁店。

segments.src: That is **recall** at work, and the brands that pop up get the first shot at your $25.
segments.tr: 这就是**回忆**在起作用，而那些率先浮现的品牌将率先获得你的 $25。

segments.src: Now picture yourself in the cereal aisle at Target.
segments.tr: 现在想象你站在塔吉特（Target）的麦片货架前。

segments.src: You didn't plan a brand, but a familiar box catches your eye and you think, "Oh, I know that one."
segments.tr: 你并没有提前计划要买哪个品牌，但一个熟悉的包装盒吸引了你的目光，你心想：“哦，我认识这个。”

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.
segments.tr: 这就是**识别**，而那个熟悉的包装有很大机会胜出，尽管一小时前你根本说不出它的名字。

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.
segments.tr: 还有那款咖啡店应用，购买达到一定次数后就送你一杯免费饮品。

segments.src: Each stamp or point is a small reward that nudges you to come back, which is operant conditioning in your pocket.
segments.tr: 每一个印章或积分都是一次小小的奖励，推动你再次光顾，这就是装在你口袋里的操作性条件反射。

segments.src: Add a cheerful seasonal ad with cozy music and fall leaves, and classical conditioning is helping too.
segments.tr: 再加上一支配有温馨音乐和秋叶画面的欢快季节性广告，经典条件反射也在起作用。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Classical conditioning links a brand to feelings by repeatedly pairing it with something people already like.
segments.tr: 1. 经典条件反射通过把品牌与人们本已喜欢的事物反复配对，将品牌与情感联系起来。

segments.src: 2. Operant conditioning shapes repeat buying through rewards such as quality, discounts, and loyalty points.
segments.tr: 2. 操作性条件反射通过质量、折扣和积分等奖励，塑造重复购买行为。

segments.src: 3. Recall (naming a brand unprompted) is harder than recognition (knowing it when you see it), and which one matters depends on where the decision happens.
segments.tr: 3. 回忆（无提示地说出品牌名）比识别（看到时认出品牌）更难，而哪一种更重要，取决于决策发生的场景。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Classical conditioning**: Learning that happens when a neutral stimulus (like a brand) is repeatedly paired with one that already triggers a response.
segments.tr: - **经典条件反射**：当中性刺激（如品牌）与一个已经能引发反应的刺激被反复配对时发生的学习。

segments.src: - **Operant conditioning**: Learning in which behavior becomes more or less likely depending on the reward or punishment that follows it.
segments.tr: - **操作性条件反射**：行为是否变得更可能或更不可能出现，取决于随之而来的奖励或惩罚的一种学习方式。

segments.src: - **Stimulus generalization**: Responding to a similar-looking stimulus the same way as to the original, such as trusting a lookalike package.
segments.tr: - **刺激泛化**：对外观相似的刺激做出与原始刺激相同的反应，例如信任一个外观相似的仿冒包装。

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: Retrieving a brand name from memory without any cue except the product category.
segments.tr: - **品牌回忆**：除了产品类别之外不借助任何线索，从记忆中提取品牌名称。

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: Correctly identifying a brand as familiar when it is shown or named.
segments.tr: - **品牌识别**：在展示或提及某个品牌时，能正确判断其为熟悉的品牌。

hi.title: [Consumer Psychology #3] उस जिंगल की धुन दिमाग में क्यों अटकी रहती है: उपभोक्ता ब्रांड कैसे सीखते और याद रखते हैं

segments.src: > Brands teach us through repeated pairings and rewards, and whether we recall a brand on our own or only recognize it on a shelf changes how we buy.
segments.tr: > ब्रांड बार-बार के जोड़ों और इनामों के ज़रिए हमें सिखाते हैं, और यह कि हम ब्रांड को खुद याद कर पाते हैं या सिर्फ़ शेल्फ़ पर देखकर पहचानते हैं, इससे बदल जाता है कि हम कैसे खरीदते हैं।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Nobody is born knowing that a red can means "refreshing" or that a swoosh means "athletic."
segments.tr: कोई भी व्यक्ति यह जानकर पैदा नहीं होता कि लाल डिब्बा "ताज़गी" का मतलब देता है या स्वूश (swoosh) चिन्ह "खेल-कूद" का।

segments.src: We **learn** these links, mostly without trying.
segments.tr: हम इन संबंधों को **सीखते** हैं, ज़्यादातर बिना कोशिश किए।

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually describe that learning in two ways.
segments.tr: उपभोक्ता मनोवैज्ञानिक आम तौर पर इस सीखने को दो तरीकों से समझाते हैं।

segments.src: Classical conditioning: learning by association**
segments.tr: शास्त्रीय अनुबंधन: संबंध जोड़कर सीखना**

segments.src: In Ivan Pavlov's famous experiments, dogs heard a sound right before getting food.
segments.tr: इवान पावलोव के प्रसिद्ध प्रयोगों में कुत्ते खाना मिलने से ठीक पहले एक आवाज़ सुनते थे।

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: कई बार ऐसा होने के बाद, अकेली वही आवाज़ सुनकर उनके मुँह में लार आने लगी।

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: विज्ञापन अक्सर इसी सिद्धांत पर काम करते हैं।

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: किसी ब्रांड (एक तटस्थ उत्तेजना) को किसी ऐसी चीज़ के साथ दिखाइए जो लोगों को पहले से अच्छा महसूस कराती है, जैसे खुशमिज़ाज संगीत, कोई प्यारा पिल्ला या मुस्कुराता हुआ मशहूर व्यक्ति, तो वह अच्छा एहसास ब्रांड पर भी कुछ हद तक चढ़ जाता है।

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: दोहराव मदद करता है, लेकिन ज़्यादा दोहराव *घिसावट* (wear-out) ला सकता है, यानी वह बिंदु जहाँ लोग ऊब जाते हैं या चिढ़ने लगते हैं।

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: इससे जुड़ा एक विचार है **उत्तेजना सामान्यीकरण** (stimulus generalization): लोग किसी एक चीज़ के प्रति अपनी भावनाएँ उससे मिलती-जुलती चीज़ों पर भी लागू कर देते हैं।

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: इसी वजह से स्टोर ब्रांड अक्सर बाज़ार के अग्रणी ब्रांड जैसी पैकेजिंग अपनाते हैं, और कोई मशहूर ब्रांड अपने नाम से नई उत्पाद श्रृंखला लॉन्च कर सकता है।

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: क्रियाप्रसूत (इंस्ट्रुमेंटल) अनुबंधन: परिणामों से सीखना**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: यहाँ व्यवहार इस बात से बनता है कि उसके *बाद* क्या होता है।

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: अगर कोई चीज़ खरीदने पर इनाम मिलता है, जैसे बढ़िया उत्पाद, छूट या लॉयल्टी पॉइंट, तो आप उसे दोबारा खरीदने के और करीब जाते हैं।

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: लॉयल्टी प्रोग्राम, "10वीं कॉफ़ी मुफ़्त" वाले पंच कार्ड और अचानक मिलने वाले फ़ायदे, ये सब इसी पर आधारित हैं।

segments.src: **Memory: recall vs.
segments.tr: **स्मृति: रिकॉल बनाम

segments.src: recognition**
segments.tr: पहचान**

segments.src: Learning only matters if it sticks.
segments.tr: सीखना तभी मायने रखता है जब वह टिके।

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:
segments.tr: विपणक ब्रांड स्मृति के दो प्रकार अलग करते हैं:

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **ब्रांड रिकॉल**: आप बिना किसी संकेत के खुद ब्रांड का नाम याद करते हैं। ("कोई राइडशेयर ऐप बताइए।")

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **ब्रांड पहचान**: आप ब्रांड को देखने या सुनने पर उसे पहचान लेते हैं। ("क्या आपने यह लोगो पहले देखा है?")

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: पहचानना याद करने से आसान है।

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: ज़्यादातर लोग बिना सुझाव के जितने ब्रांड नाम बता सकते हैं, उससे कहीं ज़्यादा ब्रांड पहचानते हैं।

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.
segments.tr: कौन-सा तरीका ज़्यादा मायने रखता है, यह इस पर निर्भर करता है कि आप फ़ैसला कहाँ लेते हैं।

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.
segments.tr: अगर आप शेल्फ़ के सामने चुनते हैं, तो पहचान काफ़ी हो सकती है।

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.
segments.tr: अगर आप बाहर जाने से पहले तय कर लेते हैं, जैसे कोई रेस्टोरेंट चुनना या प्लंबर को बुलाना, तो ब्रांड को खुद-ब-खुद दिमाग में आना होगा, इसलिए रिकॉल जीतता है।

segments.src: The few brands that come to mind for a category are sometimes called the **consideration set**.
segments.tr: किसी श्रेणी के लिए दिमाग में आने वाले चंद ब्रांड कभी-कभी **विचाराधीन समूह** (consideration set) कहलाते हैं।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Imagine it's Friday night and a friend texts, "Want to order pizza?"
segments.tr: कल्पना कीजिए शुक्रवार की रात है और एक दोस्त मैसेज करता है, "पिज़्ज़ा मंगाएँ?"

segments.src: Before opening any app, you think of maybe two or three chains.
segments.tr: कोई ऐप खोलने से पहले आप शायद दो-तीन चेन के नाम सोचते हैं।

segments.src: That is **recall** at work, and the brands that pop up get the first shot at your $25.
segments.tr: यही **रिकॉल** का काम है, और जो ब्रांड सबसे पहले याद आते हैं, उन्हें आपके $25 पर पहला मौका मिलता है।

segments.src: Now picture yourself in the cereal aisle at Target.
segments.tr: अब खुद को टारगेट के सीरियल वाले गलियारे में देखिए।

segments.src: You didn't plan a brand, but a familiar box catches your eye and you think, "Oh, I know that one."
segments.tr: आपने किसी ब्रांड की योजना नहीं बनाई थी, लेकिन एक जाना-पहचाना डिब्बा आपकी नज़र खींचता है और आप सोचते हैं, "अरे, यह तो मैं जानता हूँ।"

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.
segments.tr: यह **पहचान** है, और वह परिचित पैकेज जीत जाने की अच्छी संभावना रखता है, भले ही एक घंटे पहले आप उसका नाम न बता पाते।

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.
segments.tr: फिर वह कॉफ़ी शॉप ऐप है जो कुछ खरीद के बाद आपको एक मुफ़्त ड्रिंक देता है।

segments.src: Each stamp or point is a small reward that nudges you to come back, which is operant conditioning in your pocket.
segments.tr: हर स्टैम्प या पॉइंट एक छोटा इनाम है जो आपको वापस आने के लिए धकेलता है, यानी आपकी जेब में रखा क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन।

segments.src: Add a cheerful seasonal ad with cozy music and fall leaves, and classical conditioning is helping too.
segments.tr: इसके साथ अगर आनंदमय मौसमी विज्ञापन हो, जिसमें आरामदायक संगीत और पतझड़ के पत्ते हों, तो शास्त्रीय अनुबंधन भी मदद कर रहा है।

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
1. Classical conditioning links a brand to feelings by repeatedly pairing it with something people already like.
segments.tr: 1. शास्त्रीय अनुबंधन ब्रांड को उस चीज़ के साथ बार-बार जोड़कर भावनाओं से जोड़ता है, जो लोगों को पहले से पसंद है।

segments.src: 2. Operant conditioning shapes repeat buying through rewards such as quality, discounts, and loyalty points.
segments.tr: 2. क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन गुणवत्ता, छूट और लॉयल्टी पॉइंट जैसे इनामों के ज़रिए बार-बार खरीद को आकार देता है।

segments.src: 3. Recall (naming a brand unprompted) is harder than recognition (knowing it when you see it), and which one matters depends on where the decision happens.
segments.tr: 3. रिकॉल (बिना सुझाव के ब्रांड का नाम लेना) पहचान (ब्रांड को देखकर जानना) से कठिन है, और कौन-सा मायने रखता है, यह इस पर निर्भर करता है कि फ़ैसला कहाँ होता है।

es.title: [Psicología del Consumidor #3] Por qué ese jingle se te queda grabado en la cabeza: cómo aprenden y recuerdan las marcas los consumidores

segments.src: > Brands teach us through repeated pairings and rewards, and whether we recall a brand on our own or only recognize it on a shelf changes how we buy.
segments.tr: > Las marcas nos enseñan mediante asociaciones repetidas y recompensas, y que recordemos una marca por nuestra cuenta o solo la reconozcamos en el estante cambia la forma en que compramos.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Nobody is born knowing that a red can means "refreshing" or that a swoosh means "athletic."
segments.tr: Nadie nace sabiendo que un rojo intenso significa «refrescante» o que un swoosh significa «deportivo».

segments.src: We **learn** these links, mostly without trying.
segments.tr: Aprendemos estas asociaciones **casi siempre sin proponérnoslo**.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually describe that learning in two ways.
segments.tr: Los psicólogos del consumidor suelen describir ese aprendizaje de dos maneras.

segments.src: Classical conditioning: learning by association**
segments.tr: Condicionamiento clásico: aprendizaje por asociación**

segments.src: In Ivan Pavlov's famous experiments, dogs heard a sound right before getting food.
segments.tr: En los famosos experimentos de Ivan Pavlov, los perros oían un sonido justo antes de recibir comida.

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: Tras suficientes repeticiones, el sonido por sí solo les hacía salivar.

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: La publicidad suele funcionar con el mismo principio.

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: Muestra una marca (un estímulo neutro) junto a algo que ya hace sentir bien a la gente, como música alegre, un cachorro adorable o una celebridad sonriente, y parte de esa buena sensación puede transferirse a la marca.

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: La repetición ayuda, pero una repetición excesiva puede provocar *desgaste*, el punto en que la gente se aburre o se fastidia.

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: Una idea relacionada es la **generalización del estímulo**: las personas trasladan sus sentimientos por algo a las cosas que se le parecen.

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: Por eso las marcas blancas suelen usar envases parecidos al líder del mercado, y por eso una marca conocida puede lanzar una nueva línea de productos con el mismo nombre.

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: Condicionamiento operante (instrumental): aprendizaje por consecuencias**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: En este caso, la conducta se moldea por lo que ocurre *después*.

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: Si comprar algo lleva a una recompensa, como un buen producto, un descuento o puntos de fidelidad, es más probable que vuelvas a comprarlo.

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: Los programas de fidelidad, las tarjetas de sellos del tipo «tu décimo café es gratis» y los beneficios sorpresa se basan todos en esto.

segments.src: Learning only matters if it sticks.
segments.tr: El aprendizaje solo importa si perdura.

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:
segments.tr: Los especialistas en marketing distinguen dos tipos de memoria de marca:

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **Recuerdo de marca**: se te ocurre el nombre de la marca tú solo, sin ayuda. («Nombra una app de viajes compartidos».)

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **Reconocimiento de marca**: identificas la marca cuando la ves o la oyes. («¿Has visto antes este logotipo?»)

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: El reconocimiento es más fácil que el recuerdo.

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: La mayoría de la gente reconoce muchas más marcas de las que puede nombrar sin ayuda.

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.
segments.tr: Cuál de los dos importa más depende de dónde decidas.

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.
segments.tr: Si eliges frente a un estante, el reconocimiento puede bastar.

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.
segments.tr: Si decides antes de salir, por ejemplo al elegir un restaurante o al llamar a un fontanero, la marca tiene que venirte a la mente por sí sola, así que gana el recuerdo.

segments.src: The few brands that come to mind for a category are sometimes called the **consideration set**.
segments.tr: Las pocas marcas que se te ocurren para una categoría se llaman a veces **conjunto de consideración**.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Imagine it's Friday night and a friend texts, "Want to order pizza?"
segments.tr: Imagina que es viernes por la noche y un amigo te escribe: «¿Pedimos pizza?».

segments.src: Before opening any app, you think of maybe two or three chains.
segments.tr: Antes de abrir cualquier app, piensas en dos o tres cadenas.

segments.src: That is **recall** at work, and the brands that pop up get the first shot at your $25.
segments.tr: Eso es el **recuerdo** en acción, y las marcas que te vienen a la mente tienen la primera oportunidad con tus 25 dólares.

segments.src: Now picture yourself in the cereal aisle at Target.
segments.tr: Ahora imagina que estás en el pasillo de cereales de Target.

segments.src: You didn't plan a brand, but a familiar box catches your eye and you think, "Oh, I know that one."
segments.tr: No habías planeado ninguna marca, pero una caja conocida te llama la atención y piensas: «Ah, esa la conozco».

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.
segments.tr: Eso es **reconocimiento**, y el envase familiar tiene buenas probabilidades de ganar aunque hace una hora no habrías sabido nombrarlo.

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.
segments.tr: Luego está la app de la cafetería que te regala una bebida después de cierto número de compras.

segments.src: Each stamp or point is a small reward that nudges you to come back, which is operant conditioning in your pocket.
segments.tr: Cada sello o punto es una pequeña recompensa que te empuja a volver, que es el condicionamiento operante en tu bolsillo.

segments.src: Add a cheerful seasonal ad with cozy music and fall leaves, and classical conditioning is helping too.
segments.tr: Añade un anuncio alegre de temporada con música acogedora y hojas de otoño, y el condicionamiento clásico también ayuda.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen en 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. Classical conditioning links a brand to feelings by repeatedly pairing it with something people already like.
segments.tr: 1. El condicionamiento clásico vincula una marca con emociones al emparejarla repetidamente con algo que la gente ya aprecia.

segments.src: 2. Operant conditioning shapes repeat buying through rewards such as quality, discounts, and loyalty points.
segments.tr: 2. El condicionamiento operante moldea la recompra mediante recompensas como la calidad, los descuentos y los puntos de fidelidad.

segments.src: 3. Recall (naming a brand unprompted) is harder than recognition (knowing it when you see it), and which one matters depends on where the decision happens.
segments.tr: 3. El recuerdo (nombrar una marca sin ayuda) es más difícil que el reconocimiento (saber de ella al verla), y cuál de los dos importa más depende de dónde se toma la decisión.

segments.tr: - **استرجاع العلامة التجارية**: أن تستحضر اسم العلامة بنفسك دون أي تلميح. ("اذكر تطبيقًا لمشاركة الرحلات.")

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **التعرّف على العلامة التجارية**: أن تُعرّف على العلامة عندما تراها أو تسمعها. ("هل رأيت هذا الشعار من قبل؟")

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: التعرّف أسهل من الاسترجاع.

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: يتعرّف معظم الناس على عدد من العلامات يفوق بكثير ما يستطيعون تسميته دون تلميح.

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.

segments.tr: وتُسمّى العلامات القليلة التي تخطر ببالك لفئة معينة أحيانًا **مجموعة الاعتبار**.

fr.title: [Psychologie du consommateur #3] Pourquoi ce jingle vous trotte-t-il dans la tête : comment les consommateurs apprennent et mémorisent les marques

segments.src: > Brands teach us through repeated pairings and rewards, and whether we recall a brand on our own or only recognize it on a shelf changes how we buy.
segments.tr: > Les marques nous apprennent par des associations répétées et des récompenses, et le fait de nous souvenir d'une marque par nous-mêmes ou de simplement la reconnaître en rayon change notre façon d'acheter.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Nobody is born knowing that a red can means "refreshing" or that a swoosh means "athletic."
segments.tr: Personne ne naît en sachant qu'un rouge vif signifie « rafraîchissant » ou qu'un swoosh signifie « sportif ".

segments.src: We **learn** these links, mostly without trying.
segments.tr: Nous **apprenons** ces liens, le plus souvent sans effort.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually describe that learning in two ways.
segments.tr: Les psychologues de la consommation décrivent généralement cet apprentissage de deux façons.

segments.src: Classical conditioning: learning by association**
segments.tr: Conditionnement classique : apprendre par association**

segments.src: In Ivan Pavlov's famous experiments, dogs heard a sound right before getting food.
segments.tr: Dans les célèbres expériences d'Ivan Pavlov, des chiens entendaient un son juste avant de recevoir de la nourriture.

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: Après un nombre suffisant d'associations, le son seul suffisait à les faire saliver.

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: La publicité fonctionne souvent sur le même principe.

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: Montrez une marque (un stimulus neutre) à côté de quelque chose qui plaît déjà, comme une musique entraînante, un chiot mignon ou une célébrité souriante, et une partie de ce sentiment agréable peut déteindre sur la marque.

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: La répétition aide, mais une répétition excessive peut provoquer *l'usure*, le moment où les gens s'ennuient ou s'agacent.

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: Une idée connexe est la **généralisation du stimulus** : les gens transfèrent leurs sentiments envers une chose vers les choses qui lui ressemblent.

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi les marques de distributeurs adoptent souvent un emballage qui ressemble à celui du leader du marché, et pourquoi une marque connue peut lancer une nouvelle gamme de produits sous le même nom.

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: Conditionnement opérant (instrumental) : apprendre par les conséquences**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: Ici, le comportement est façonné par ce qui se passe *après* lui.

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: Si l'achat de quelque chose mène à une récompense, comme un excellent produit, une remise ou des points de fidélité, vous devenez plus susceptible de le racheter.

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: Les programmes de fidélité, les cartes à tampons du type « votre 10e café est offert » et les avantages surprise reposent tous sur ce principe.

segments.src: **Memory: recall vs.
segments.tr: **Mémoire : rappel vs.

segments.src: recognition**
segments.tr: reconnaissance**

segments.src: Learning only matters if it sticks.
segments.tr: L'apprentissage ne compte que s'il reste en mémoire.

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:
segments.tr: Les spécialistes du marketing distinguent deux types de mémoire de marque :

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **Rappel de marque** : vous retrouvez le nom de la marque vous-même, sans indice. (« Citez une application de covoiturage. »)

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **Reconnaissance de marque** : vous identifiez la marque lorsque vous la voyez ou l'entendez. (« Avez-vous déjà vu ce logo ? »)

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: La reconnaissance est plus facile que le rappel.

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: La plupart des gens reconnaissent bien plus de marques qu'ils ne peuvent en citer spontanément.

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.
segments.tr: Lequel compte le plus dépend de l'endroit où l'on décide.

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.
segments.tr: Si vous choisissez devant un rayon, la reconnaissance peut suffire.

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.
segments.tr: Si vous décidez avant de sortir, par exemple pour choisir un restaurant ou appeler un plombier, la marque doit venir à l'esprit toute seule, donc le rappel l'emporte.

segments.src: The few brands that come to mind for a category are sometimes called the **consideration set**.
segments.tr: Les quelques marques qui viennent à l'esprit pour une catégorie sont parfois appelées l'**ensemble de considération**.

segments.tr: Imaginez un vendredi soir : un ami vous envoie un texto : « On commande une pizza ? »

segments.src: Before opening any app, you think of maybe two or three chains.
segments.tr: Avant d'ouvrir la moindre application, vous pensez à deux ou trois chaînes tout au plus.

segments.src: That is **recall** at work, and the brands that pop up get the first shot at your $25.
segments.tr: C'est le **rappel** à l'œuvre, et les marques qui surgissent en premier ont la première chance de recevoir vos 25 $.

segments.src: Now picture yourself in the cereal aisle at Target.
segments.tr: Imaginez maintenant que vous êtes dans le rayon céréales d'un Target.

segments.src: You didn't plan a brand, but a familiar box catches your eye and you think, "Oh, I know that one."
segments.tr: Vous n'aviez pas prévu de marque, mais une boîte familière attire votre regard et vous pensez : « Ah, celle-là, je la connais. »

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.
segments.tr: C'est la **reconnaissance**, et l'emballage familier a de bonnes chances de l'emporter, même si vous n'auriez pas pu la citer une heure plus tôt.

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.
segments.tr: Il y a aussi l'application d'un café qui vous offre une boisson gratuite après un certain nombre d'achats.

segments.src: Each stamp or point is a small reward that nudges you to come back, which is operant conditioning in your pocket.
segments.tr: Chaque tampon ou point est une petite récompense qui vous incite à revenir : c'est le conditionnement opérant dans votre poche.

segments.src: Add a cheerful seasonal ad with cozy music and fall leaves, and classical conditioning is helping too.
segments.tr: Ajoutez une publicité saisonnière joyeuse avec une musique douce et des feuilles d'automne, et le conditionnement classique aide aussi.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en 3 lignes

segments.src: 1. Classical conditioning links a brand to feelings by repeatedly pairing it with something people already like.
segments.tr: 1. Le conditionnement classique relie une marque à des sentiments en l'associant de façon répétée à quelque chose que les gens apprécient déjà.

segments.src: 2. Operant conditioning shapes repeat buying through rewards such as quality, discounts, and loyalty points.
segments.tr: 2. Le conditionnement opérant façonne les achats répétés grâce à des récompenses telles que la qualité, les remises et les points de fidélité.

segments.tr: 3. Le rappel (citer une marque spontanément) est plus difficile que la reconnaissance (la connaître quand on la voit), et lequel compte dépend de l'endroit où la décision se prend.

segments.tr: Nos famosos experimentos de Ivan Pavlov, os cães ouviam um som logo antes de receber comida.

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: Depois de pareamentos suficientes, o som sozinho já fazia os cães salivarem.

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: A publicidade costuma funcionar com o mesmo princípio.

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: Mostre uma marca (um estímulo neutro) ao lado de algo que já deixa as pessoas bem, como música animada, um filhote fofo ou uma celebridade sorridente, e parte dessa sensação positiva pode passar para a marca.

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: A repetição ajuda, mas repetir demais pode causar *desgaste*, o ponto em que as pessoas ficam entediadas ou irritadas.

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: Uma ideia relacionada é a **generalização de estímulo**: as pessoas transferem o que sentem por algo para coisas parecidas com ele.

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: É por isso que marcas próprias de lojas costumam usar embalagens parecidas com a líder de mercado, e por que uma marca conhecida pode lançar uma nova linha de produtos com o mesmo nome.

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: Condicionamento operante (instrumental): aprendizado por consequências**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: Aqui, o comportamento é moldado pelo que acontece *depois* dele.

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: Se comprar algo leva a uma recompensa, como um ótimo produto, um desconto ou pontos de fidelidade, você fica mais propenso a comprar de novo.

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: Programas de fidelidade, cartões de carimbo do tipo "seu 10º café é grátis" e vantagens surpresa são todos baseados nisso.

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **Lembrança de marca**: você chega ao nome da marca sozinho, sem nenhuma pista. ("Cite um aplicativo de transporte.")

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **Reconhecimento de marca**: você identifica a marca ao vê-la ou ouvi-la. ("Você já viu este logotipo antes?")

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: O reconhecimento é mais fácil do que a lembrança.

segments.tr: Se você decide antes de sair, por exemplo ao escolher um restaurante ou chamar um encanador, a marca precisa vir à mente por conta própria, então a lembrança é que vence.

segments.tr: Você não tinha escolhido uma marca, mas uma caixa familiar chama sua atenção e você pensa: "Ah, conheço esse."

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.

segments.src: > Brands teach us through repeated pairings and rewards, and whether we recall a brand on our own or only recognize it on a shelf changes how we buy.
segments.tr: > ブランドは繰り返しの組み合わせと報酬を通じて私たちに学習させ、ブランドを自力で思い出すか、棚でただ見分けるだけかによって、購買行動は変わります。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日の概念

segments.src: Nobody is born knowing that a red can means "refreshing" or that a swoosh means "athletic."
segments.tr: 赤い缶が「さわやか」を意味するとか、スウッシュ（ナイキのロゴ）が「スポーティー」を意味するとかは、生まれながらに知っている人はいません。

segments.src: We **learn** these links, mostly without trying.
segments.tr: 私たちはこうした結び付きを、ほとんどの場合意識せずに**学習**しています。

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually describe that learning in two ways.
segments.tr: 消費者心理学者は通常、この学習を2つの方法で説明します。

segments.src: Classical conditioning: learning by association**
segments.tr: 古典的条件付け：連想による学習**

segments.src: In Ivan Pavlov's famous experiments, dogs heard a sound right before getting food.
segments.tr: イワン・パブロフの有名な実験では、犬は餌をもらう直前に音を聞かされました。

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: 十分に組み合わせを繰り返すと、音だけで犬は唾液を分泌するようになりました。

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: 広告も同じ原理でよく機能します。

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: ブランド（中立的な刺激）を、陽気な音楽、かわいい子犬、笑顔の有名人など、すでに人を心地よくさせるものと一緒に見せると、その心地よさの一部がブランドにも移ることがあります。

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: 繰り返しは効果がありますが、繰り返しすぎると*ウェアアウト*（飽きや煩わしさを感じる段階）を招くことがあります。

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: 関連する考え方が**刺激般化**です。人は、ある対象に抱いた感情を、それに似た見た目の対象にも持ち越します。

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: そのため、プライベートブランド商品はしばしばトップブランドに似たパッケージを用い、知名度の高いブランドは同じ名前で新しい製品ラインを発売できるのです。

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: オペラント（道具的）条件付け：結果による学習**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: ここでは、行動はその後に起こることによって形づくられます。

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: 何かを買うことが、優れた製品、割引、ポイントなどの報酬につながると、同じものをまた買う可能性が高まります。

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: ロイヤルティプログラム、「10杯目のコーヒー無料」のスタンプカード、サプライズ特典はいずれもこの原理に基づいています。

segments.src: **Memory: recall vs.
segments.tr: **記憶：再生 vs.

segments.src: recognition**
segments.tr: 再認**

segments.src: Learning only matters if it sticks.
segments.tr: 学習は定着してこそ意味があります。

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:
segments.tr: マーケターはブランド記憶を2種類に区別します：

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **ブランド再生**：何のヒントもなしに、自分でブランド名を思い出すこと。（「配車アプリを挙げてください」）

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **ブランド再認**：ブランドを見たり聞いたりしたときに、それだと見分けること。（「このロゴを見たことがありますか？」）

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: 再認は再生より簡単です。

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: ほとんどの人は、ヒントなしで挙げられるよりはるかに多くのブランドを見分けられます。

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.
segments.tr: どちらがより重要かは、どの場面で決めるかによります。

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.
segments.tr: 棚の前で選ぶなら、再認だけで十分かもしれません。

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.
segments.tr: 外出前に決めるなら、たとえばレストランを選ぶ場合や水道業者に電話する場合、ブランドは自分で思い浮かぶ必要があるので、再生が勝ります。

segments.src: The few brands that come to mind for a category are sometimes called the **consideration set**.
segments.tr: あるカテゴリーで真っ先に思い浮かぶ少数のブランドは、**検討集合**と呼ばれることもあります。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活の中で

segments.src: Imagine it's Friday night and a friend texts, "Want to order pizza?"
segments.tr: 金曜の夜、友人から「ピザ頼まない？」とメッセージが来た場面を想像してください。

segments.src: Before opening any app, you think of maybe two or three chains.
segments.tr: どのアプリを開くより前に、おそらく2〜3のチェーン店を思い浮かべます。

segments.src: That is **recall** at work, and the brands that pop up get the first shot at your $25.
segments.tr: これが**再生**の働きで、すぐに思い浮かんだブランドが、あなたの25ドルを獲得する最初のチャンスを得るのです。

segments.src: Now picture yourself in the cereal aisle at Target.
segments.tr: 次に、Targetのシリアル売り場にいる自分を思い浮かべてください。

segments.src: You didn't plan a brand, but a familiar box catches your eye and you think, "Oh, I know that one."
segments.tr: ブランドを決めていなかったのに、見慣れた箱が目に留まり、「あ、これ知ってる」と思います。

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.
segments.tr: これが**再認**で、1時間前には名前を挙げられなかったとしても、見慣れたパッケージは選ばれる可能性が高いのです。

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.
segments.tr: また、一定回数の購入後に無料ドリンクがもらえるコーヒーショップのアプリもあります。

segments.src: Each stamp or point is a small reward that nudges you to come back, which is operant conditioning in your pocket.
segments.tr: スタンプやポイントはそれぞれ小さな報酬で、また来店するよう背中を押します。これはポケットの中で働くオペラント条件付けです。

segments.src: Add a cheerful seasonal ad with cozy music and fall leaves, and classical conditioning is helping too.
segments.tr: 心地よい音楽と紅葉をあしらった明るい季節限定の広告を加えると、古典的条件付けも一役買っています。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3行まとめ

segments.src: 1. Classical conditioning links a brand to feelings by repeatedly pairing it with something people already like.
segments.tr: 1. 古典的条件付けは、人がすでに好んでいるものとブランドを繰り返し組み合わせることで、ブランドと感情を結び付ける。

segments.src: 2. Operant conditioning shapes repeat buying through rewards such as quality, discounts, and loyalty points.
segments.tr: 2. オペラント条件付けは、品質、割引、ポイントなどの報酬を通じて、リピート購入を形づくる。

segments.src: 3. Recall (naming a brand unprompted) is harder than recognition (knowing it when you see it), and which one matters depends on where the decision happens.
segments.tr: 3. 再生（ヒントなしにブランド名を挙げること）は再認（見たときにそれだと分かること）より難しく、どちらが重要かは決定が行われる場面によって変わる。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Classical conditioning**: Learning that happens when a neutral stimulus (like a brand) is repeatedly paired with one that already triggers a response.
segments.tr: - **古典的条件付け**：中立的な刺激（ブランドなど）を、すでに反応を引き起こす刺激と繰り返し組み合わせたときに起こる学習。

segments.src: - **Operant conditioning**: Learning in which behavior becomes more or less likely depending on the reward or punishment that follows it.
segments.tr: - **オペラント条件付け**：その後に続く報酬や罰によって、行動が起こりやすくなったり起こりにくくなったりする学習。

segments.src: - **Stimulus generalization**: Responding to a similar-looking stimulus the same way as to the original, such as trusting a lookalike package.
segments.tr: - **刺激般化**：よく似た刺激に対して、元の刺激と同じように反応すること。たとえば、よく似たパッケージを信頼するなど。

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: Retrieving a brand name from memory without any cue except the product category.
segments.tr: - **ブランド再生**：製品カテゴリー以外の手がかりなしに、記憶からブランド名を取り出すこと。

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: Correctly identifying a brand as familiar when it is shown or named.
segments.tr: - **ブランド再認**：ブランドが提示されたり名前を挙げられたりしたときに、それを見慣れたものとして正しく見分けること。

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 (b).
segments.tr: *解答：Q1 (b)。

segments.src: The ad pairs the brand with an already pleasant scene so the good feeling transfers, which is classical conditioning.
segments.tr: この広告は、ブランドをすでに心地よい場面と組み合わせて、良い感情を移し替えているので、古典的条件付けです。

segments.src: Q2 X.
Recognition is easier, because the cue (logo, package, name) is right in front of you; recall requires retrieving the brand with no cue.
segments.tr: 再認の方が簡単です。手がかり（ロゴ、パッケージ、名前）が目の前にあるからです。再生は手がかりなしでブランドを取り出す必要があります。

segments.src: When you decide before seeing any options, the brand has to come to mind on its own.
segments.tr: 選択肢を一つも見ずに決める場合、ブランドは自分で思い浮かばなければなりません。

segments.src: At a checkout counter or store shelf, recognition does most of the work.*
segments.tr: レジや店の棚では、再認がほとんどの役割を果たします。*

segments.src: - **Classical conditioning**: Learning that happens when a neutral stimulus (like a brand) is repeatedly paired with one that already triggers a response.
segments.tr: - **Klassische Konditionierung**: Lernen, das stattfindet, wenn ein neutraler Reiz (etwa eine Marke) wiederholt mit einem Reiz gepaart wird, der bereits eine Reaktion auslöst.

segments.src: - **Operant conditioning**: Learning in which behavior becomes more or less likely depending on the reward or punishment that follows it.
segments.tr: - **Operante Konditionierung**: Lernen, bei dem Verhalten je nach der darauf folgenden Belohnung oder Strafe wahrscheinlicher oder unwahrscheinlicher wird.

segments.src: - **Stimulus generalization**: Responding to a similar-looking stimulus the same way as to the original, such as trusting a lookalike package.
segments.tr: - **Reizgeneralisierung**: Auf einen ähnlich aussehenden Reiz so reagieren wie auf das Original, etwa einer Nachahmer-Verpackung vertrauen.

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: Retrieving a brand name from memory without any cue except the product category.
segments.tr: - **Markenerinnerung (Recall)**: Einen Markennamen aus dem Gedächtnis abrufen, ohne einen anderen Hinweis als die Produktkategorie.

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: Correctly identifying a brand as familiar when it is shown or named.
segments.tr: - **Markenwiedererkennung (Recognition)**: Eine Marke korrekt als vertraut identifizieren, wenn sie gezeigt oder genannt wird.

vi.title: [Consumer Psychology #3] Vì sao điệp khúc ấy cứ quanh quẩn trong đầu bạn: Người tiêu dùng học và ghi nhớ thương hiệu như thế nào

segments.src: > Brands teach us through repeated pairings and rewards, and whether we recall a brand on our own or only recognize it on a shelf changes how we buy.
segments.tr: > Thương hiệu dạy chúng ta qua những cặp kích thích lặp lại và phần thưởng, và việc chúng ta tự nhớ ra một thương hiệu hay chỉ nhận ra nó khi thấy trên kệ hàng sẽ thay đổi cách chúng ta mua sắm.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Nobody is born knowing that a red can means "refreshing" or that a swoosh means "athletic."
segments.tr: Không ai sinh ra đã biết rằng màu đỏ có nghĩa là "sảng khoái" hay dấu móc (swoosh) có nghĩa là "thể thao".

segments.src: We **learn** these links, mostly without trying.
segments.tr: Chúng ta **học** những liên kết này, phần lớn không cần cố gắng.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually describe that learning in two ways.
segments.tr: Các nhà tâm lý học tiêu dùng thường mô tả quá trình học này theo hai cách.

segments.src: Classical conditioning: learning by association**
segments.tr: Điều kiện hóa cổ điển: học qua liên tưởng**

segments.src: In Ivan Pavlov's famous experiments, dogs heard a sound right before getting food.
segments.tr: Trong thí nghiệm nổi tiếng của Ivan Pavlov, những con chó nghe một âm thanh ngay trước khi được cho ăn.

segments.src: After enough pairings, the sound alone made them salivate.
segments.tr: Sau đủ số lần ghép cặp, chỉ riêng âm thanh đó cũng khiến chúng tiết nước bọt.

segments.src: Advertising often works on the same principle.
segments.tr: Quảng cáo thường vận hành theo nguyên tắc tương tự.

segments.src: Show a brand (a neutral stimulus) next to something that already makes people feel good, like upbeat music, a cute puppy, or a smiling celebrity, and some of that good feeling can rub off on the brand.
segments.tr: Hiển thị một thương hiệu (kích thích trung tính) cùng với thứ vốn đã khiến người ta thấy dễ chịu, như âm nhạc vui tươi, chú chó con đáng yêu hay người nổi tiếng đang cười, và một phần cảm giác dễ chịu ấy có thể lan sang thương hiệu.

segments.src: Repetition helps, but too much repetition can cause *wear-out*, the point where people get bored or annoyed.
segments.tr: Lặp lại có tác dụng, nhưng lặp lại quá nhiều có thể gây *wear-out* (suy giảm hiệu quả), tức là thời điểm mọi người bắt đầu chán hoặc khó chịu.

segments.src: A related idea is **stimulus generalization**: people carry their feelings about one thing over to things that look like it.
segments.tr: Một ý tưởng liên quan là **khái quát hóa kích thích**: người ta mang cảm xúc về một thứ sang những thứ trông giống nó.

segments.src: This is why store brands often use packaging that resembles the market leader, and why a well-known brand can launch a new product line under the same name.
segments.tr: Đây là lý do các nhãn hàng riêng của siêu thị thường dùng bao bì giống với thương hiệu dẫn đầu thị trường, và vì sao một thương hiệu nổi tiếng có thể tung ra dòng sản phẩm mới dưới cùng một tên.

segments.src: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: learning by consequences**
segments.tr: Điều kiện hóa thao tác (công cụ): học qua hệ quả**

segments.src: Here, behavior is shaped by what happens *after* it.
segments.tr: Ở đây, hành vi được hình thành bởi những gì xảy ra *sau* khi nó diễn ra.

segments.src: If buying something leads to a reward, like a great product, a discount, or loyalty points, you become more likely to buy it again.
segments.tr: Nếu việc mua một món đồ dẫn đến phần thưởng, như sản phẩm tốt, giảm giá hay điểm tích lũy, bạn sẽ có nhiều khả năng mua lại món đó.

segments.src: Loyalty programs, "your 10th coffee is free" punch cards, and surprise perks are all built on this.
segments.tr: Chương trình khách hàng thân thiết, thẻ tích điểm kiểu "ly cà phê thứ 10 miễn phí" và các ưu đãi bất ngờ đều dựa trên nguyên tắc này.

segments.src: **Memory: recall vs.
segments.tr: **Trí nhớ: nhớ lại (recall) so với

segments.src: recognition**
segments.tr: nhận diện (recognition)**

segments.src: Learning only matters if it sticks.
segments.tr: Việc học chỉ có ý nghĩa khi nó được ghi nhớ lâu.

segments.src: Marketers distinguish two kinds of brand memory:
segments.tr: Các nhà marketing phân biệt hai loại trí nhớ thương hiệu:

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: you come up with the brand name yourself, with no prompt. ("Name a rideshare app.")
segments.tr: - **Brand recall (nhớ lại thương hiệu)**: bạn tự nghĩ ra tên thương hiệu mà không cần gợi ý. ("Hãy kể tên một ứng dụng gọi xe.")

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: you identify the brand when you see or hear it. ("Have you seen this logo before?")
segments.tr: - **Brand recognition (nhận diện thương hiệu)**: bạn xác định được thương hiệu khi nhìn thấy hoặc nghe thấy. ("Bạn đã từng thấy logo này chưa?")

segments.src: Recognition is easier than recall.
segments.tr: Nhận diện dễ hơn nhớ lại.

segments.src: Most people recognize far more brands than they can name unprompted.
segments.tr: Hầu hết mọi người nhận diện được nhiều thương hiệu hơn số lượng họ có thể tự kể tên mà không có gợi ý.

segments.src: Which one matters more depends on where you decide.
segments.tr: Loại nào quan trọng hơn tùy thuộc vào nơi bạn đưa ra quyết định.

segments.src: If you choose in front of a shelf, recognition may be enough.
segments.tr: Nếu bạn chọn ngay trước kệ hàng, nhận diện có thể là đủ.

segments.src: If you decide before you go out, for example picking a restaurant or calling a plumber, the brand has to come to mind on its own, so recall wins.
segments.tr: Nếu bạn quyết định trước khi ra ngoài, chẳng hạn chọn nhà hàng hay gọi thợ sửa ống nước, thương hiệu phải tự xuất hiện trong đầu, nên nhớ lại sẽ quan trọng hơn.

segments.src: The few brands that come to mind for a category are sometimes called the **consideration set**.
segments.tr: Vài thương hiệu xuất hiện trong đầu khi nghĩ đến một danh mục được gọi là **tập hợp cân nhắc** (consideration set).

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong đời sống hằng ngày

segments.src: Imagine it's Friday night and a friend texts, "Want to order pizza?"
segments.tr: Hãy hình dung đó là tối thứ Sáu và một người bạn nhắn tin: "Đặt pizza không?"

segments.src: Before opening any app, you think of maybe two or three chains.
segments.tr: Trước khi mở bất kỳ ứng dụng nào, bạn nghĩ đến có lẽ hai hoặc ba chuỗi.

segments.src: That is **recall** at work, and the brands that pop up get the first shot at your $25.
segments.tr: Đó là **nhớ lại** đang hoạt động, và những thương hiệu hiện ra trước sẽ có cơ hội đầu tiên với 25 đô la của bạn.

segments.src: Now picture yourself in the cereal aisle at Target.
segments.tr: Giờ hãy tưởng tượng bạn đang đứng ở quầy ngũ cốc tại Target.

segments.src: You didn't plan a brand, but a familiar box catches your eye and you think, "Oh, I know that one."
segments.tr: Bạn không định sẵn thương hiệu nào, nhưng một hộp quen thuộc thu hút ánh nhìn và bạn nghĩ "À, mình biết hộp này."

segments.src: That is **recognition**, and the familiar package has a good chance of winning even though you couldn't have named it an hour ago.
segments.tr: Đó là **nhận diện**, và bao bì quen thuộc có khả năng cao thắng thế dù một giờ trước bạn không thể kể tên nó.

segments.src: Then there's the coffee shop app that gives you a free drink after a certain number of purchases.
segments.tr: Rồi đến ứng dụng quán cà phê tặng bạn một ly đồ uống miễn phí sau một số lần mua nhất định.

segments.src: Each stamp or point is a small reward that nudges you to come back, which is operant conditioning in your pocket.
segments.tr: Mỗi con dấu hay điểm tích lũy là một phần thưởng nhỏ thúc bạn quay lại, đó chính là điều kiện hóa thao tác ngay trong túi bạn.

segments.src: Add a cheerful seasonal ad with cozy music and fall leaves, and classical conditioning is helping too.
segments.tr: Thêm một quảng cáo mùa lễ vui tươi với âm nhạc ấm cúng và lá thu, thì điều kiện hóa cổ điển cũng đang góp sức.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. Classical conditioning links a brand to feelings by repeatedly pairing it with something people already like.
segments.tr: 1. Điều kiện hóa cổ điển gắn thương hiệu với cảm xúc bằng cách lặp lại việc ghép thương hiệu với thứ mọi người vốn đã thích.

segments.src: 2. Operant conditioning shapes repeat buying through rewards such as quality, discounts, and loyalty points.
segments.tr: 2. Điều kiện hóa thao tác định hình việc mua lặp lại thông qua phần thưởng như chất lượng, giảm giá và điểm tích lũy.

segments.src: 3. Recall (naming a brand unprompted) is harder than recognition (knowing it when you see it), and which one matters depends on where the decision happens.
segments.tr: 3. Nhớ lại (tự kể tên thương hiệu không cần gợi ý) khó hơn nhận diện (biết thương hiệu khi nhìn thấy), và loại nào quan trọng phụ thuộc vào nơi quyết định diễn ra.

segments.tr: - **Điều kiện hóa cổ điển**: Việc học diễn ra khi một kích thích trung tính (như thương hiệu) được lặp lại ghép cặp với một kích thích đã sẵn gây ra phản ứng.

segments.src: - **Operant conditioning**: Learning in which behavior becomes more or less likely depending on the reward or punishment that follows it.
segments.tr: - **Điều kiện hóa thao tác**: Việc học trong đó hành vi trở nên có khả năng xảy ra nhiều hơn hoặc ít hơn tùy thuộc vào phần thưởng hay hình phạt đi kèm sau đó.

segments.src: - **Stimulus generalization**: Responding to a similar-looking stimulus the same way as to the original, such as trusting a lookalike package.
segments.tr: - **Khái quát hóa kích thích**: Phản ứng với một kích thích có hình dạng tương tự giống như với kích thích gốc, chẳng hạn tin tưởng một bao bì giả giống.

segments.src: - **Brand recall**: Retrieving a brand name from memory without any cue except the product category.
segments.tr: - **Nhớ lại thương hiệu**: Truy xuất tên thương hiệu từ trí nhớ mà không có gợi ý nào ngoài danh mục sản phẩm.

segments.src: - **Brand recognition**: Correctly identifying a brand as familiar when it is shown or named.
segments.tr: - **Nhận diện thương hiệu**: Xác định đúng một thương hiệu là quen thuộc khi nó được hiển thị hoặc được nêu tên.
